Paint one illustration of a single moment from The Holy Bible.

RULES (they outrank everything below):
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) A subject without form is never drawn. Only the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind the moment names may stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the moment names who sits on it.
8) A character you draw from CANON keeps exactly that look. Anyone else the moment needs appears as an unnamed figure with an ordinary, different face.

MOMENT (Daniel 6:22): "My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me, because innocence was found in me before him; and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”"

CONTEXT (for understanding only; paint the moment above):
- Before: Then Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!
- After: Then the king was exceedingly glad, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

HOW TO READ IT: choose the single instant that best shows what happens in the moment and paint that, as if the viewer stands inside the scene. When someone speaks, show the speaker and listeners where they are; never paint the content of the speech as a separate scene or as figures beside them. Figures of speech and comparisons are not literal objects. Infer place, time, light and weather from the text and context.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return
People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.
Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.
Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

CANON, NAMED HERE (fixed look; the moment decides pose, expression, clothing changes and action):
- Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man, grave and greying; olive-brown skin; close-cropped greying hair and a short trimmed grey beard; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.

CANON, ELSEWHERE IN THIS PASSAGE (draw one only when the moment involves them, for example as "he" or "they"; otherwise leave them out):
- Darius the Mede: early sixties; broad, settled build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and hair under a tall royal cap; lined, steady face with heavy brows. Signature outfit: a long purple court robe over a cream tunic, with a gold-embroidered collar and a deep blue sash. Signature prop: a signet ring of gold on his right hand.
- The den of lions: a deep circular stone pit cut into bare earth beside a royal enclosure, its walls of dressed grey limestone rising high above a sandy floor. A heavy wooden lid and an iron-banded gate sit at the rim, reached by a worn stone stair. Dry scrub and a few palms grow at the edge; no plants inside the pit.

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached in this order; identity and rendering only, never composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject and layout.
- Image 2: Daniel's reference sheet (one figure in several views). Keep Daniel's identity exactly; do not copy its poses, layout or plain background.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted differently.

- Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

- the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. CONTEXT (for understanding only; paint the moment above):
- Before: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
- After: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”

Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

Signature outfit: a undyed linen tunic and a rough brown wool cloak with fringed hem. Signature props: a fishing net coiled over one shoulder for Peter and Andrew; a walking staff for travelers.

MOMENT (1 Samuel 17:49): "David put his hand in his bag, took a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the earth."

CONTEXT (for understanding only; paint the moment above):
- Before: When the Philistine arose, and walked and came near to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
- After: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him; but there was no sword in David’s hand.

CANON, NAMED HERE (fixed look; the moment decides pose, expression, clothing changes and action):
- David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

CANON, ELSEWHERE IN THIS PASSAGE (draw one only when the moment involves them, for example as "he" or "they"; otherwise leave them out):
- Goliath: man of enormous height, over nine feet tall, broad-shouldered and heavily muscled, around forty years old. Olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a full dark beard, strong heavy brow, grave and hard features. Wears bronze scale armour over a linen tunic, bronze greaves, and a bronze helmet, colours of bronze, dark leather and undyed linen. Carries a great spear with a heavy iron head and a sword at his side.
- Saul: a man in his forties, tall and broad-shouldered with a strong, weathered face, dark hair cut to the neck and a short, close beard. Skin olive-brown from sun. Dignified, brooding eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of deep blue wool under a dark red royal cloak with a gold-bordered hem, a bronze-scaled leather belt and a plain sandal. Carries a royal spear of dark ash wood with a bronze head.
- Abner son of Ner: a man of middle to later years, broad-shouldered and sturdy, with a dignified, weathered face. Skin olive-brown from the sun. Hair dark, graying at the temples, worn to the shoulder; a short, close-cut grey-streaked beard. Wears a long undertunic and a cloak of deep blue over bronze scale armour, with a leather sword belt. Carries a long spear and a bronze-hilted sword.
- Philistines: adult men of the coastal cities, age twenty to forty; medium-to-broad build, sun-browned skin; close-cropped dark hair and a short beard; calm, hard-set features, not caricatured. Typical dress: a knee-length woven tunic of undyed wool with a bordered hem in blue or red, a leather belt and a short cloak of dark wool. Signature props: a bronze helmet with a crest and a round shield, carried by the army; no props carried by the figure alone.
- Valley of Elah: a broad, shallow valley of the Judean lowlands between rounded hills of terraced limestone, with a dry watercourse winding through its floor. Scattered terebinth and oak trees and low scrub grow along the slopes, and sun-baked earth shows pale between rocks. Rough stone walls and simple dwellings of field stone mark the hill ridges.
- Gath: a fortified Philistine city on a low hill of the Shephelah, reached by a dusty road from the lowland fields. Thick mudbrick and stone city walls crowned with timber towers, a broad gate of heavy timber and bronze fittings, and tall stone-and-mudbrick houses with flat roofs clustered inside. Olive groves, terraced vineyards and grain fields spread beyond the walls; sycamore and terebinth stand along the road. Cult stands and a temple precinct rise above the houses.
